ἀδελφός.long: a brother, member of the same religious community, especially a fellow-Christian.
ἀδελφός.sd: a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like G1 (Α))
ἀδελφός.der: from G1 (Α) (as a connective particle) and (the womb);
ἀδελφός.as:
ἀδελφός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ἀ- copul., δελφύς, womb),
in cl., a brother, born of the same parent or parents. [In LXX (Hort, Ja., 102 f.), for אָח;]
1. lit. of a brother (Ge 4:2, al.).
2. Of a neighbour (Le 19:17).
3. Of a member of the same nation (Ex 2:14, De 15:3). In NT in each of these senses (1. Mt 1:2, al.; 2. Mt 7:3; 3. Ro 9:3) and also,
4. of a fellow-Christian: I Co 1:1, Ac 9:30. This usage finds illustration in π., where ἀ. is used of members of a pagan religious community (M, Th., I, 1:4; MM, VGT, s.v.). The ἀδελφοὶ τ. Κυρίου (Mt 12:46-4913:5528:10, Mk 3:31-34, Lk 8:19-21, Jo 2:127:3, 51020:17, Ac 1:14, I Co 9:5) may have been sons of Joseph and Mary (Mayor, Ja., Intr. viff.; DB, i, 320 ff.) or of Joseph by a former marriage (Lft., Gal., 252ff.; DCG, i, 232 ff.), but the view of Jerome, which makes ἀ. equivalent to ἀνεψιός, is inconsistent with Greek usage. (Cremer, 66.)

ἄδικος.sd: unjust; by extension wicked; by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen
ἄδικος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1349 (δίκη);
ἄδικος.as:
ἄδικος, -ον
(< δίκη), [in LXX for שׁקר, עול, etc.;]
1.unjust: Ro 3:5, He 6:10.
2.unrighteous, wicked: Lk 16:1118:11, Ac 24:15, I Co 6:1, 9I Pe 3:18; opp. to δίκαιος, Mt 5:45; to εὐσεβής, II Pe 2:9; to πιστός, Lk 16:10 (Cremer, 200).†

ᾅδης.sd: properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls
ᾅδης.der: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1492 (εἴδω);
ᾅδης.as:
ᾅδης, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX ehiefly for שְׁאוֹל, also for דּוּמָה, מָוֶת, etc.;]
1. in Hom., Hades (Pluto), the god of the underworld.
2.the abode of Hades, the underivorld; in NT, the abode of departed spirits, Hades: ἐν τ. ᾅ., Lk 16:23; εἰς ᾅ., Ac 2:27, 31; πύλαι ᾅδου, Mt 16:18; κλεῖς τοῦ ᾅ., Re 1:18; metaph., ἕως ᾅ., Mt 11:23, Lk 10:15; personified, Re 6:820:13, 14 (Cremer, 67, 610; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀδελφή.long: a sister, a woman (fellow-)member of a church, a Christian woman.
ἀδελφή.as:
ἀδελφή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ἀδελφός), [in LXX for אָחוֹת;]
a sister: Mt 19:29, al.; metaph. (MM, VGT, s.v.), of a member of the Christian community: Ro 16:1, I Co 7:15Ja 21:15, al.

ἀδυνατέω.long: to be impossible; I am unable.
ἀδυνατέω.as:
ἀδυνατέω, -ῶ
(< ἀδύνατος), [in LXX: De 17:8, Za 8:6 (פּלא ni.), Jb 42:2 (בּצר ni.), al.;]
1.Abbott-Smith omits this numberto be unable (cl., Philo; π., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).
2. In LXX and NT (Kennedy, Sources, 124; Hatch, Essays, 4; Field, Notes, 46 f.), to be impossible: Mt 17:20, Lk 1:37.†

ἀδύνατος.long: of persons: incapable; of things: impossible; either the inability, or that which is impossible.
ἀδύνατος.sd: unable, i.e. weak (literally or figuratively); passively, impossible
ἀδύνατος.kj: could not do, impossible, impotent, not possible, weak
ἀδύνατος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1415 (δυνατός);
ἀδύνατος.as:
ἀ-δύνατος, -ον,
[in LXX for אֶבְיוֹן, דַּל, etc.;]
1. of persons, unable, powerless: Ac 14:8; fig. Ro 15:1 (MM, VGT, s.v.).
2. Of things, impossible: Mt 19:26, Mk 10:27, Lk 18:27, Ro 8:3, He 6:4, 1810:411:6.†

ἀδικέω.long: I act unjustly towards, injure, harm.
ἀδικέω.sd: to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or physically)
ἀδικέω.kj: hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer, take) wrong
ἀδικέω.as:
ἀδικέω, -ῶ
(< ἄδικος), [in LXX for עשׁק, עוה, etc.;]
1. intrans., to be ἄδικος, do wrong, act wickedly or criminally: Ac 25:11, I Co 6:8, II Co 7:12, Col 3:25, Re 22:11; to do hurt, Re 9:19.
2. Trans.
(a)to do some wrong: ὃ ἠδίκησεν, Col 3:25; to wrong some one, Mt 20:13, Ac 7:26, 2725:10, II Co 7:2, Ga 4:12, Phm 18, II Pe 2:13; pass., Ac 7:24, II Co 7:12; mid., I Co 6:7 (suffer . . . to be wronged; WM, §38, 3; but v. Bl., §54, 5; and cf. ἀποστερέω);
(b)to injure, hurt: Lk 10:19Re 2:116:67:2, 39:4, 1011:5.†

ἀδημονέω.long: I feel fear, lack courage, am distressed, troubled.
ἀδημονέω.kj: be full of heaviness, be very heavy
ἀδημονέω.der: from a derivative of (to be sated to loathing);
ἀδημονέω.as:
** ἀδημονέω, -ῶ (on the derivation, v. MM, VGT, s.v.), [in Aq.: Jb 18:20; Sm.: Ps 60 (61):3115:2 (116:11), Ec 7:17(16), Ez 3:15*;]
to be troubled, distressed (MM, l.c.): Mt 26:37, Mk 14:33, Phl 2:26.†

Ἀδδί.long: Addi, son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

Ἀδάμ.long: Adam, the first man, the first parent of the human race.
Ἀδάμ.sd: Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative)
Ἀδάμ.as:
Ἀδάμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָדָם),
Adam: Lk 3:38, Ro 5:14, I Co 15:22, 45, I Ti 2:13, 14Ju 14. Christ ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀ., I Co 15:45.†

ἄδηλος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1212 (δῆλος);
ἄδηλος.as:
ἄ-δηλος, -ον
(< δῆλος), [in LXX: Ps 50 (51):6 (בַּטֻּחוֹת);]
1.unseen, unobserved, not manifest (Ps 50 (51):6): Lk 11:44.
2.uncertain, indistinct: I Co 14:8.†

ἀδικία.sd: (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act)
ἀδικία.as:
ἀδικία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἄδικος), [in LXX for עָוֹן, פֶּשַׁע, עָוֶל, etc.;]
1.injustice: Lk 18:6, Ro 9:14.
2.unrighteousness, iniquity: Jo 7:18, Ac 8:23, Ro 1:18, 292:86:13, II Ti 2:19, I Jo 1:95:17; opp. to ἀλήθεια, I Co 13:6, II Th 2:12; to δικαιοσύνη, Ro 3:5; ἀπάτη τῆς ἀ., II Th 2:10; μισθὸς ἀδικίας, Ac 1:18, II Pe 2:13, 15; ἐγράται τῆς ἀ., Lk 13:27; μαμωνᾶς τῆς ἀ., Lk 16:9; κόσμος τῆς ἀ., Ja 3:6; οἰκονόμος τῆς ἀ., Lk 16:8.
3. = ἀδίκημα, an unrighteous act: ironically, a favour, II Co 12:13; pl., He 8:12 (Cremer, 261; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀδίκημα.long: a legal wrong, crime (with which one is charged), misdeed, crime against God, a sin.
ἀδίκημα.kj: evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong
ἀδίκημα.as:
ἀδίκημα, -τος, τό
(< ἀδικέω), [in LXX for עָוֹן, פֶּשַׁע, etc.;]
a wrong, injury, misdeed (MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 18:1424:20, Re 18:5.†

Ἀδραμυττηνός.long: belonging to Adramyttium, a port in Mysia, in Asia Minor.
Ἀδραμυττηνός.as:
Ἁδραμυντηνός (T, Rec. Ἀδραμυττηνός), -ή,-όν,
of Adramyttium, a seaport of Mysia: Ac 27:2.†

Ἀδρίας.long: the Hadria, a name given by sailors not merely to the Adriatic Sea, to which it properly belonged, but also to the open Mediterranean to the south-east of Italy, to the sea that lay between Malta, Italy, Greece, and Crete.
Ἀδρίας.as:
Ἁδρίας (T, Rec. Ἀδρίας), -ου, ὁ,
the Adriatic sea, in later Greek usage extended to take in all the waters between Greece and Italy: Ac 27:27.†

ἀδιαλείπτως.sd: uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an appropriate occasion)
ἀδιαλείπτως.as:
**† ἀδιαλείπτως (v. supr.), adv.,
[in LXX: I Mac 12:11, II Mac4, III Mac 6:33*;]
unremittingly, incessantly: Ro 1:9, I Th 1:32:135:17.†

ἀδόκιμος.long: failing to pass the test, unapproved, counterfeit.
ἀδόκιμος.sd: unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally)
ἀδόκιμος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1384 (δόκιμος);
ἀδόκιμος.as:
ἀ-δόκιμος, -ον,
[in LXX: Pr 25:4, Is 1:22 (סִיג)*;]
1. of things (prop. of metals: LXX, Pr 25:4, Is 1:22), not standing the test, rejected: γῆ, He 6:8.
2. Of persons, rejected after testing, reprobate: Ro 1:28, I Co 9:27, II Co 13:5-7, II Ti 3:8, Tit 1:16 (Cremer, 212).†

ἀδιάλειπτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of G1223 (διά) and G3007 (λείπω);
ἀδιάλειπτος.as:
*† ἀδιάλειπτος, -ον
(< διαλείπω),
unremitting, incessant: Ro 9:2, II Ti 1:3. (For exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.)†

ἀδάπανος.long: without expense, for which nothing has to be paid.
ἀδάπανος.as:
* ἀδάπανος, -ον
(< δαπάνη),
without expense, free of charge: I Co 9:18.†

ἀδήλως.long: out of sight, obscurely, inconspicuously, uncertainly, without certain aim.

ἁδρότης.as:
* ἁδρότης, -τος, ἡ
(< ἁδρός, thick, well-grown),
1.thickness, vigour.
2.abundance, bounty: II Co 8:20.†

ᾄδω.as:
ᾄδω (Attic form of Ion. and poët. ἀείδω),
[in LXX chiefly for שִׁיר;]
to sing,
(a) intrans., c. dat. (MM, VGT, s.v.), of praise to God: Eph 5:19, Col 3:16;
(b) trans., c. cogn. acc.: ᾠδὴν, Re 5:914:315:3.†

ἀδηλότης.long: the quality of being unseen (of disappearing), indefiniteness, uncertainty.

ἀδιάκριτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1252 (διακρίνω);
ἀδιάκριτος.as:
ἀ-διά-κριτος, -ον
(< διακρίνω), [in LXX: Pr 25:1*;]
1.not to be parted, mixed, undistinguishable (cf. Pr 25:1, and v. Lft., Ignat. Eph., §3).
2.without uncertainty (Hort, in l., but v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Ja 3:17.†

ἄδολος.as:
* ἄδολος, -ον,
1.guileless (Pind., Thuc).
2. Of liquids (Æsch., Eur., and late prose writers), genuine, pure (in π. and in MGr. of wine, also of corn: MM, VGT, s.v.; Milligan, NTD, 77): of milk, metaph., I Pe 2:2.†
SYN.: ἀκέραιος (q.v.), ἄκακος, ἁπλοῦς.

ἀδελφότης.long: brotherhood (in the collective sense), the members of the Christian Church, Christendom.
ἀδελφότης.sd: brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity
ἀδελφότης.as:
**† ἀδελφότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< ἀδελφός), [in LXX: I Mac 12:10, 17, IV Mac5*;]
1. abstract, brotherhood, brotherly affection (LXX).
2. Concrete, the brotherhood, the Christian community: I Pe 2:175:9 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀδίκως.as:
ἀδίκως, adv.
(< ἄδικος), [in LXX for שׁקר, עול, etc.;]
unjustly, undeservedly: I Pe 2:19.†
